statuses.verified: The main claim is supported by the listed source.
statuses.verified_with_note: The main claim is supported, but wording needs context or the metric is limited.
statuses.needs_follow_up: The entry should not be promoted until the source or wording is improved.
statuses.corrected: The entry was changed after verification found a problem.

checks.evidence: UNEP reports that the ozone layer is on track to recover following global phase-down of ozone-depleting substances.
checks.note: Keep the wording about recovery as a projected path, not a completed repair.

checks.evidence: WHO states that smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980 after global vaccination and surveillance work.
checks.note: Strong entry; source directly supports the claim.

checks.evidence: UNICEF Data reports a large decline in the global under-five mortality rate between 1990 and 2024.
checks.note: The entry uses an approximate percentage, which is appropriate for TRMNL copy.

checks.evidence: UNICEF Data reports that 961 million people gained access to safely managed drinking water services between 2015 and 2024.
checks.note: Strong metric, but the caveat should remain because billions still lack safely managed service.

checks.evidence: Our World in Data shows a major long-term decline in extreme poverty from 1990 to recent estimates.
checks.note: Use approximate values and keep the caveat; recent estimates can shift with new World Bank data.

checks.evidence: Our World in Data documents the long-run rise in literacy from a small historical minority to a large modern majority.
checks.note: This is a broad historical trend, not a precise single-year claim.

checks.evidence: UNAIDS reports that AIDS-related deaths have fallen substantially from the 2004 peak and from 2010 levels.
checks.note: The entry avoids overclaiming by not saying AIDS is solved.

checks.evidence: UNICEF Data reports that the global maternal mortality ratio declined by about 40 percent from 2000 to 2023.
checks.note: Strong entry; the caveat correctly keeps preventable deaths visible.

checks.evidence: IEA reports that renewables supplied about 32 percent of global electricity in 2024 and projects continued growth.
checks.note: Do not generalize this to total energy; the entry correctly says electricity.

checks.evidence: UNEP reports that the last country using leaded petrol phased it out in 2021, ending legal road use worldwide.
checks.note: Strong repair story with an important legacy-pollution caveat.

checks.evidence: Our World in Data shows that global death rates from total air pollution have declined sharply since 1990.
checks.note: The driver is mainly reduced indoor air pollution; keep that qualifier in the summary.

checks.evidence: WWF reports that mountain gorilla numbers have recovered to more than 1,000 individuals in the wild.
checks.note: Strong conservation entry; retain endangered-status caveat.

checks.evidence: WHO reports that wild poliovirus cases have decreased by more than 99 percent since 1988.
checks.note: Do not call polio eradicated; the current wording is correct.

checks.evidence: The Carter Center reports a decline from about 3.5 million annual human cases in 1986 to 10 human cases in 2025.
checks.note: Very strong repair entry; the animal-reservoir caveat is important.

checks.evidence: WHO reports that 32 countries had been validated as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem by July 2026.
checks.note: Elimination as a public health problem is a technical threshold, not total disappearance.

checks.evidence: WHO reports five countries verified as free of onchocerciasis after elimination activities.
checks.note: The entry is country-specific; avoid implying global elimination.

checks.evidence: WHO/UNICEF JMP reports that the number of people practising open defecation declined from 1.3 billion in 2000 to 419 million in 2022.
checks.note: Strong infrastructure entry with a clear remaining-burden caveat.

checks.evidence: UNICEF and ILO report that child labour has almost halved since 2000, from 246 million to 138 million children.
checks.note: Keep the caveat prominent because the world missed the elimination target.

checks.evidence: EPA reports that annual sulfur dioxide emissions from U.S. power plants fell by 95 percent from 1995 to 2023.
checks.note: This is a U.S. power-sector claim, not a global acid-rain claim.

checks.evidence: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service reports recovery from hundreds of breeding pairs in the 1960s to 9,789 nesting pairs by 2007.
checks.note: Strong story; keep the location limited to the lower 48 states.

checks.evidence: IUCN reports an increase from 62 mature Iberian lynx in 2001 to 648 in 2022, with total population estimated above 2,000.
checks.note: Strong conservation entry; threats remain serious.

checks.evidence: WWF reports that giant pandas were downlisted after a 17 percent population increase over a decade.
checks.note: Downlisted does not mean safe; habitat fragmentation remains a real risk.

checks.evidence: Protected Planet reports 2024 coverage of 17.6 percent of terrestrial and inland waters and 8.4 percent of marine and coastal areas.
checks.note: Coverage alone does not prove effective conservation management.

checks.evidence: WHO reports annual road traffic deaths fell slightly to 1.19 million, about 5 percent below 2010.
checks.note: This is a modest repair; the title correctly says 'slightly'.
